# IP-blocking solutions — generated tables

Cost and effectiveness normalized to ONE workload: 10,000 successful fetches per month of Cloudflare-protected pages, ~500 KB each (~5 GB egress), 20% needing a persistent session, driven from Jod's VPS. Per-IP options are costed at 10 IPs; browser-hour options at 25 hours/month.

55 candidates, 50 eligible after filters.
Monte Carlo: 20,000 trials perturbing **success rate** (not price) by each
row's confidence, plus weights +/-35%.

## Weighting — Jod profile

- **effectiveness** — 30%
- **cost** — 25%
- **completeness** — 20%
- **integration** — 10%
- **ethics** — 10%
- **ops** — 5%

behaviour, IP reputation, CAPTCHA) the solution addresses. It is the column
that explains most of the surprises in this table.

## Layer coverage by category

| Category | Typical layers fixed | Reading |
|---|---:|---|
| baseline | 1.0 / 6 | the starting point — fails before the IP is even considered |
| datacenter | 0.0 / 6 | changes nothing Cloudflare scores |
| residential | 1.0 / 6 | fixes the IP only; the TLS handshake still gives you away |
| isp | 1.0 / 6 | fixes the IP only, but flat-rate and consented |
| mobile | 1.0 / 6 | fixes the IP only, at the highest trust level available |
| self-hosted | 3.7 / 6 | fixes the client fingerprint; add an IP source for the rest |
| browser-infra | 4.6 / 6 | managed client fingerprint, IP sometimes billed separately |
| unblocker-api | 5.7 / 6 | the whole chain, priced per request |

Rows marked `composed-estimate` are stacks whose success rate was inferred by
combining two separately-measured components. No benchmark tested those
pairings; they are the study's central recommendation *and* its least certain
numbers, which is why the Monte Carlo perturbs them hardest.
